Antibodies against Echinococcus spp. were presented in the routinary and confirmatory analyses, respectively, ELISA and IB.

report.source_text: The abdominal ultrasound (US) and CT completion exam revealed an additional giant cyst in the liver with a maximum size of 16 cm (Figure 1). Clinical and radiological investigations performed via chest radiography and TC (Figure 1) showed two cystic lesions with the typical feature of echinococcal cysts in both lungs and a third one in the liver. According to the WHO, the hepatic cyst was staged as CE3a via US examination.

report.source_text: Given the worsening symptomatology due to the septic scenario sustained by empyema in the right pleural cavity, the patient was referred to a tertiary thoracic surgery department for management. A right thoracotomy surgery, with video-thoracoscopic assistance, was performed to remove the cyst, reduce the infectious burden, and perform a pleural debridement. Despite clinical improvement, a redo-surgery was necessary to repair a bronchopleural fistulation one week later. After completely recovering the right pleuropulmonary side, the hydatid cyst on the left lung, which also ruptured into bronchioles, was treated surgically using a total minimally invasive technique (Figure 2). The patient was discharged on postoperative day 23 after the first operation.

clinician.final_diagnosis: CE caused by the zoonotic parasite E. granulosus s.s. of the G1 genotype
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old woman with exposure to farm animals and unwashed vegetables presented with progressive weight loss, intermittent fever, abdominal distension, chest pain, dyspnea, cough, vomiting, and fever. Serological testing confirmed antibodies against Echinococcus spp. Imaging (US and CT) identified cystic lesions typical of echinococcal cysts in liver (CE3a stage) and lungs. Molecular RT-PCR analysis confirmed E. granulosus sensu stricto, G1 genotype. The clinical course involved thoracotomy with cyst removal and pleural debridement, followed by redo surgery for bronchopleural fistula repair, and a minimally invasive procedure for the contralateral cyst. The patient was discharged after full recovery.
